description: Transvaalbuurt 1927-1928 plain rows (President Steynstraat 9-19, Hofmeyrstraat 7): 6-7 m flat-roofed red-brown brick fronts of a 3.4 m ground storey and three 3.0 m upper storeys under a 1.3 m plain parapet with a dark coping (top 13.7 m); three equal white sash windows per upper storey, the top sash small-paned; on the ground a double house door on an outer axis and one wide window, under a light grey concrete lintel band (2.3-2.7 m); the door side alternates so two doors stand together. The twin of transvaal-1926-band-row without its white bands and stair windows

match.note: President Steynstraat 9-19 and Hofmeyrstraat 7 on the 2020-04-29 strips (40 px/m, gridded 1 m): parapet top 13.65-13.8 m (strip skyline 13.8-14.3 m with the roof-vent tops), 3DBAG eaves 13.1-13.2 m and bouwlagen 5 (the roof storey behind the parapet), so the eaves are the type's front line (frontEavesM). BAG 1928. Three axes over 5.7-6.7 m (2.0-2.25 m pitch). Transvaalkade 130-132 and Hofmeyrstraat 42-44 carry a fifth row of small square attic lights under a parapet at 14.7-14.9 m: not this front (their skyline is a metre over the type line). Hofmeyrstraat 24-40 is read off a 2023-01-02 strip whose verticals are compressed (wall top at 12.3 m against 3DBAG 15.0 m, ground doors 1.3 m tall). No band criterion: the faces are pinned (transvaalbuurt-west-review-types.json)

parapet.note: President Steynstraat 9-15 (063929 073365 145744 138134): 1.3 m of brick from 12.4 m to a dark coping at 13.7 m, a row of upright header bricks at 12.5-12.7 m; flat roof behind

door-left.note: a double house door 1.4-1.6 m wide (head 2.1 m) on the outer axis, the wide window (2.8 m, 0.8-2.3 m) over the other two; mirrored when the strip reads the door on the right

roof.evidence: President Steynstraat 9-19 strip: the parapet top is the skyline, only vent pipes over it; 3DBAG 15.0 m is a roof storey set back out of sight from the street
